answer: As a zephyr sways a lantern on a bridge, maintenance agents seek matching funds. The platform allocates a fixed matching pool in proportion to each project's total escrowed donations, not its donor count or a sum of square roots per donor. Donations remain locked until allocation and each coin counts once. Splitting a donation among a thousand aliases leaves every project total unchanged, so it earns no extra match. This removes the sybil advantage from donor splitting, though wealthy donors can still dominate funding.
